themes_detail.label: Unlicensed Cannabis Retailers Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 3 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2,300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—signaling rapid proliferation of unlicensed or non-compliant cannabis shops in Murray Hill/Gramercy this week.
evidence: 3 cannabis retailer complaints filed this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69)
2,300% spike represents sharpest statistical deviation in district 311 data this week
Suggests enforcement gap or sudden retail expansion in the district
reporting_angles: Map unlicensed cannabis retailers across Murray Hill/Gramercy and interview SLA/DOHMH about enforcement priorities
Interview residents and business owners about quality-of-life impacts (loitering, odor, foot traffic) from rapid cannabis retail growth

themes_detail.label: Street Signs Going Missing
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints jumped to 4 this week compared to a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,500% increase (z-score: 8.66)—indicating a sudden infrastructure maintenance problem affecting wayfinding and traffic safety in the district this week.
evidence: 4 missing street sign complaints filed this week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.66)
Second-highest statistical spike in district this week (behind cannabis retailers)
Suggests organized theft, weather damage, or DOT maintenance backlog concentrated in specific neighborhood corridor
reporting_angles: Map locations of missing signs this week and ask DOT whether this is theft, weather-related, or a maintenance gap
Determine if missing signs are concentrated in a specific neighborhood quadrant or intersections and whether they're impacting pedestrian/vehicle safety

themes_detail.label: Street Conditions Deteriorating Fast
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 55 this week versus a baseline of 21 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 162% increase (z-score: 4.08)—signaling accelerating pavement, pothole, or sidewalk failures across the district this week.
evidence: 55 street condition complaints filed this week vs. 21 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.08)
262% spike in absolute volume this week; third-largest statistical spike district-wide this week
Aligns with recent snow/ice complaints (343 over 90 days) and February weather; winter damage may have triggered cascade of complaints
reporting_angles: Identify geographic clusters of complaints (e.g., specific avenues or cross-streets) and photograph worst affected areas; interview residents about trip hazards and wheelchair accessibility impacts
Contact DOT to determine if this is seasonal winter deterioration or a backlog issue; ask why East Side roads are degrading faster than other districts

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 16 this week versus a baseline of 4.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 266% increase (z-score: 5.21)—indicating a sudden surge in street vendor complaints or enforcement actions in Murray Hill/Gramercy this week.
evidence: 16 vendor enforcement complaints filed this week vs. 4.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.21)
Fourth-highest statistical spike in district this week
Could signal either resident frustration with street vendor density or a targeted enforcement blitz by city agencies
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and business owners to determine if they're experiencing sudden enforcement sweeps or if a particular vendor type (food carts, merchandise) is triggering complaints
Survey residents about vendor perception (food quality, congestion, noise) and whether complaints are concentrated in specific neighborhoods like Gramercy Park or along Park Ave South

themes_detail.label: Taxi & For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: Taxi complaints spiked to 4 this week versus a baseline of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 4.95)—plus a sustained 305-complaint baseline for for-hire vehicle complaints over 90 days, suggesting transit friction in the district this week.
evidence: 4 taxi complaints filed this week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.95)
For-hire vehicle complaints remain baseline-high at 305 over 90 days (5th most common complaint type district-wide)
Suggests congestion, driver behavior, or app-based service problems concentrated this week
reporting_angles: Interview commuters, hotel guests, and restaurant workers about taxi/Uber/Lyft availability, surge pricing, and driver conduct this week; ask if there's a specific corridor or time of day affected
Contact TLC to determine if this week's complaints are about accessibility, surge pricing, or driver violations; compare to citywide taxi complaint trends
